investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The pod remained unscheduled for 136–144 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and violating all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that are eligible by affinity/selector. No VM slot was available to schedule the agent pod, so the pod remained in Unschedulable state for the full eval window. Because the pod never started, the runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completed, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was written. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the production Kubernetes cluster; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader user-facing outage.

[Possible] Cluster under-provisioning: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-eligible nodes may have insufficient total VM capacity for concurrent eval runs plus any production workloads sharing the same resource.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The pod remained unscheduled for 136–144 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and violating all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that are eligible by affinity/selector. No VM slot was available to schedule the agent pod, so the pod remained in Unschedulable state for the full eval window. Because the pod never started, the runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completed, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was written. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the production Kubernetes cluster; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader user-facing outage.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-28 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node cluster had only 2 nodes eligible for kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads, both of which reported insufficient VM capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. When the eval runner called createAgent for a "remote" agent type (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the resulting pod was placed in the Unschedulable state for 144 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the pod never started, no agent was created, no runtime response was obtained, and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) remained missing. The same scheduling failure independently blocked remote-agent-create (136 s unscheduled) and remote-agent-state (144 s unscheduled), confirming the constraint is at the cluster/node-pool layer rather than in the eval runner logic itself.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: both nodes have consumed their full VM slot allocation, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes carry, so even if VM slots were freed the other 4 nodes could never accept the pod. This is a structural constraint that limits burst capacity.

Tertiary — a prior eval run or concurrent workload consumed the available VM slots and did not release them before this run started: the three checks ran sequentially (create ended at 14:19, state ended at 14:21, runtime ended at 14:24) and each found zero available slots, suggesting slots were not freed between runs.

Lower confidence — a node or VM pool scaling event reduced available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below the minimum needed for eval pods: no node-pool or infrastructure change evidence is present in the packet, so this remains speculative.

A successful re-run of the eval immediately after this failure, with no change to cluster capacity, would suggest the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly held slot was released) rather than a sustained exhaustion.

Cluster node-pool logs showing a scale-up event completing successfully during the eval window, with pods still failing to schedule, would suggest a quota or limit-range cap above the node level is the true constraint.
